name: THE BOUNTIFUL NUGGET (CANDIDATE)
note: Doc 05 Room 3 plus doc 16, verbatim. Twelve hotspots and two exits. THE HANDBILL is the Rules of the Assay and carries Rule 3. THE PATRONS has no drawn figures in the background -- doc 07's ambient characters supply them at runtime, so the rect covers where they stand. Doc 16 note 4: the stove's third LISTEN reverses the first two on purpose; it has gone out and nobody has noticed. Do not 'correct' it.

LOOK_AT.say: A hand of cards, face up, abandoned. It is a very good hand.
repeat: Still there. Nobody has claimed it and nobody has cleared it.
I have decided he is coming back. I have decided this several times.
then: Somebody left a very good hand on a table and went outside.

repeat: Nothing.
Nothing. Whoever he was, he is not in the building.

overrides.USE: I do not play. My father was very clear about it, and he was wrong about most things.

LISTEN_TO.say: Paper. It has been on this wall a long time. It has stopped being read.
repeat: Paper. Still not being read.
Nothing. It has outlasted everyone who nailed it up.

LOOK_AT.say: RULES OF THE ASSAY. One: a man may not be interrupted in his account. Two: a man's account may be doubted only by a better one. Three: truth is admissible but has never been raised. Four: the judges' decision is final and may be appealed to the same judges. Five: no firearms, no knives, no arithmetic.
repeat: I have read it twice. Rule five forbids arithmetic, which I assume has a history.
Rule four permits an appeal to the same judges who made the decision. Somebody thought about that and wrote it down anyway.

overrides.PICK_UP: It has been nailed on. Thoroughly. Somebody wanted the rules to stay up.

LOOK_AT.say: A spittoon, positioned optimistically far from anyone sitting down.
repeat: The floor around it tells the story of a town that has tried.
Brass. Somebody polished this once, as a joke or as a duty.
Still yes.
I have stopped.

LOOK_AT.say: A portrait of a man in a good collar, hung crooked, above a saloon.
repeat: The three answers were a governor, a founder, and 'that's Bill's uncle.'
It is the same photograph the Clarion prints as Obadiah Mott. I am fairly sure. I am not going to raise it.
then: Nobody in here knows who he is. I have asked three people and had three answers.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. He has been silent about it for years.
repeat: Nothing.
Nothing. He is a man in Ohio and nobody is asking him.

lit.note: THE FIRE, LIFTED OUT OF THE PLATE as its own layer (Phase 1.5): the base plate's firebox is cold iron; this overlay is the fire the accepted plate painted, alpha-cut, drawn over it while the stove is lit. Phase 2's flicker animates THIS layer and nothing in the plate. 'A cast iron stove, lit, in July.'

out.note: Doc 16, THE STOVE LISTEN 3: 'Nothing. It has gone out and nobody has noticed.' Nothing is drawn: the base plate's cold firebox shows, the stove's runtime pool and its mover field are gated off (lamps.stove.whenObject). No trigger sets this state in Act I yet; the architecture holds it, and ?objects=stove=out shows it.

LOOK_AT.say: A cast iron stove, lit, in July.
repeat: Still lit. There is a man beside it who has not taken his coat off since I arrived in this territory.
The warmest thing in Consolation, wasted on a room full of men who are already drinking.
then: Nobody has raised it and I am not going to be the first.

LISTEN_TO.say: It ticks. It is the only object in this room doing honest work.
repeat: Ticking. Working.
Nothing. It has gone out and nobody has noticed.

overrides.OPEN: It is lit. I am not opening a lit stove in a wooden building full of drunk men.

LOOK_AT.say: A chandelier. Below it, a dirt floor. The two have never been introduced.
repeat: Brass, crystal, and a dirt floor. Somebody made a decision about priorities and I should like to meet them.
It is not lit. It has never been lit while I have been in this room.
Ticking as it cools. Still hanging over mud.
Nothing. It is the most expensive object in the territory and it has nothing to say for itself.
then: It is the most expensive object in the territory and it is hanging over mud.

overrides.PULL: It is nine feet up and it weighs more than I do. I shall admire it from here.

LOOK_AT.say: A window onto Main Street, and the cleanest thing in the building, because it is the only thing anyone in here looks at.
repeat: From in here the street looks better. That is what a window is for.
Somebody has scratched a name into the pane. It is not a name I know.

LISTEN_TO.say: The street. Muffled. Somebody arguing about a boundary.
repeat: Still the boundary. Still arguing.
The stage has come in. Four days from Sacramento and eleven new men who think they are early.

LOOK_AT.say: An upright, hauled four hundred miles by mule, at a cost exceeding its value by an order of magnitude. Nobody here can play it.
repeat: Nobody has touched it since I arrived. I check.
There is a bottle ring on the lid. Several. It is being used as furniture.

LISTEN_TO.say: C-sharp is a semitone flat and has been for years. Nobody has noticed.
repeat: Still C-sharp. Still flat. Still nobody.
I could put it right in four minutes, and I have begun to think about it during other activities.
then: I have made a note of it. I have made several notes of it.

overrides.USE: I could tune it. Nobody has asked me, and I have decided that asking to be asked is beneath me.
overrides.OPEN: The lid comes up. Inside is a piano, which is what I expected and somehow still a disappointment.

LOOK_AT.say: Stairs, up to rooms I have not been invited to. There is a man on the landing.
repeat: He has not moved. I have begun to suspect he is not waiting for anything.
Eleven steps. I have counted them from down here, which is as far as I have got.
then: There is always a man on the landing.

LISTEN_TO.say: Boards, above. Somebody pacing a room about the size of mine.
repeat: Still pacing.
He has stopped. That is somehow worse.

overrides.USE: I have not been invited up and I am not going to invite myself.

LOOK_AT.say: I look like a man who has recently been robbed and is being brave about it.
repeat: Still me. I had hoped for some improvement.
Eleven weeks, and I have started to look like I belong here, which was not the plan.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. Mirrors are silent, which is the only restraint they show.
repeat: Still nothing.
Nothing. I keep checking. It keeps not.

LOOK_AT.say: Nine men drinking after dark, all of whom were at their claims by seven this morning and will be again by seven tomorrow. This is the part in between.
repeat: The same nine. I have started to be able to tell them apart, which I regard as a poor sign.
Nobody in here is talking about anything but where the gold is. They have been having this conversation for twelve years and it has not advanced.

LISTEN_TO.say: Talk. A great deal of it, all at the same volume, none of it listened to.
repeat: Somebody in the corner has told the same story four times and it has grown twice.
The word 'Mott' comes up about once a minute. I have counted. It is once a minute.

overrides.TALK_TO: I have tried. They are very friendly, and they want to know what I know, and I know nothing, and this disappoints them each time.

LOOK_AT.say: Mahogany. Genuinely. Somebody spent real money on the one surface everyone leans on.
repeat: Mahogany. Four hundred miles from a tree that could have produced it.
The only maintained surface in Consolation, and it is a bar.
Glasses. Talk. The same story, larger.
Somebody is being served ahead of somebody else and it is being noticed.
then: Somebody in the corner has told the same story four times and it has grown twice.

overrides.PUSH: It does not move. It is the only thing in Consolation built to stay.

LOOK_AT.say: Batwing doors, from the inside. They swing both ways, which from in here reads as a warning rather than a convenience.
repeat: The street past them. It is always a surprise.
Six inches of boardwalk and then the mud. I know exactly how far it is now.

LISTEN_TO.say: The street. It sounds busier from in here than it is.
repeat: Boots on the boardwalk. Somebody deciding whether to come in.
Nothing. Everyone who is coming in is in.

LOOK_AT.say: A door behind the bar, shut. There is a room back there and things are settled in it.
repeat: Shut. It has been shut every time I have looked, which is not the same as locked.
A door behind the bar. Shut, and shut in a way that has been decided rather than just closed.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. Whatever happens back there happens quietly, and then everyone agrees about it.
repeat: A pencil. Somebody is writing something down.
Two men going in. A little later, two men coming out, and one of the two is pleased.

overrides.PUSH: It gives half an inch and stops. Somebody has a chair against it.

entrances.note: Through the batwing doors on the left wall, facing right into the room.
Anything else arrives by the door.

castNote: No ambient sprites: the seven men are baked into the four whole plates. Nothing is composited, so nothing can drift.

lamps.note: The wall lamp between the doors and the window, the one the candidate paints lit. Small, and the only light on the street wall.

A fire in an iron box. It flickers hardest and fastest. Re-declared on the candidate at the stove's own position (the shipping declaration sat 235 px left of its drawn stove). GATED ON THE STOVE'S OBJECT STATE (Phase 1.5): out means no pool and no field.
The two wall lamps behind the bar, together, at their painted positions (1520,210 and 1850,170). Barely moving -- trimmed, because the barman is the only person in town who maintains anything.

walkBoxNote: GENERATED by tools/compile-room.mjs from reference/room-03-candidate/annotation.json. Heights come from that annotation’s own depth curve, which each room derives from its own architecture -- doc 36 Q10.
retiredNote:
THE 320x144 RELICS ARE GONE. This room carried an `idles` layer declaring four 18-pixel figures against a sheet drawn for the retired 320x144 presentation, and a foreground plane of the same vintage -- both drawn into a 1920x864 room, which is what put black boxes on the floor and one beside Thad. They described the same men who are now baked into the plates: the bar’s near and middle drinkers, a seated player, and doc 16’s man beside the stove.
THE MAN ON THE LANDING SURVIVES THE DELETION, because he was never in that list. Ruling 20 makes him an explicit exception -- his whole joke is that he never moves -- and doc 16 keeps him in THE STAIRS: there is always a man on the landing.

occlusionProofs.note: Directly behind the spittoon and 24 px above its base. The brass stands at 745-864 and he stands at 800, so it crosses him from the knee down -- 4% of the figure, which is the whole of what a spittoon should take and is exactly what he drew straight over before this plane was cut. TWO POINTS WERE DROPPED FROM THIS LIST and the reason is worth keeping: one stood in the same band 200 px along, where the mask is transparent, and the check refuses a point claiming an occlusion its mask cannot produce; the other stood in front of the brass at plane 0, and a plane a room does not declare cannot be proved. There is in any case no walkable ground DIRECTLY in front of the spittoon -- its obstacle runs from y 824 to the frame's foot, which is phase 2A's correction and stands.

occlusionPlanes.note: The spittoon, authored as a polygon because it cannot be thresholded: in the band around it the brass runs luminance 19-84 against dirt at 31-51 and warmth 44-64 against 45-53, which is the same lamps lighting both. tools/retrofit/nugget-spittoon-mask.py, --check draws it back over the art.

population.note: ROOM 3 REBUILD (Tyler, 2026-09-11). THE NUGGET'S POPULATION IS NINE AND SEVEN OF THEM ARE PAINT. The owner ruled the four card players and the three bar men into the background art as static staging, keeping only the landing man and the stove man as runtime actors, and the count therefore stopped being something a test could get by counting ambient files. This declares it instead: every one of the nine, what he is doing, whether he is paint or an actor, and where he is in the plate -- boxes read off art/staging/room-03/rebuild-01/plate-room-03-rebuilt.png on a 50 px grid. A person can check it against renders/opening-set-retrofit/room-03-rebuild-population.webp in under a minute, and tests/phase2a-access.test.ts checks the arithmetic every run.

people.what: flat cap, nearest the piano, back three-quarters to camera, holding a fanned hand
grey hair and side-whiskers, far side of the table, facing the room, holding a fanned hand
the young one in shirtsleeves and a blue neckerchief, far side, facing the room, holding a fanned hand
bald, spectacles, nearest the stove, back to camera, holding a fanned hand
SEATED: the old bearded miner, hips on the far stool, one boot on its ring, both forearms on the counter, tin cup
LEANING: the lean younger man in shirtsleeves, waistcoat and watch chain, forearm taking his weight on the counter top, both boots on the dirt

STANDING: the heavy moustached man in the bowler and checked shirt, tin mug in hand, half turned into the room, both boots on the dirt with the brass foot rail passing behind them. TRANSLATED 82 ROWS DOWN on 2026-09-12: the endpoint had stood him on the bar's own kick-board, 70 to 95 px above the floor.
there is always a man on the landing, and he has not moved
coat buttoned to the throat, both hands open toward the iron, turned into the stove, AT THE BACK OF THE ROOM beside it and behind the card group
